result.title: Precision-Aware Learning Rate Transfer Across Block Count in LLM Post-Training
result.summary: The post-training of pretrained large language models, including supervised finetuning (SFT), direct preference optimization (DPO), and reinforcement learning with verifiable reward (RLVR), is very sensitive to the learning rate, and tuning it through grid search is costly in both computation and memory. In this work, we propose \textbf{TipSweep}, a method to transfer the learning rate across the number of trainable transformer blocks. To do so efficiently, we search for the best learning rate by training only the last $k_0$ blocks (in our experiments, typically $k_0=1$), and provide scaling rules that predict the optimal learning rate when training any set of $k$ blocks, including when $k=L$ (the full transformer). Across experiments with models ranging from 1 to 7 billion parameters, we observe that the optimal learning rate follows precision-dependent scaling rules: the optimal rate scales approximately as $k^{-1}$ with float32 (FP32) master weights, but as $k^{-1/2}$ when updates are applied directly to bfloat16 (BF16) weights without a master copy. We explain both rules using an analytical model that accounts for update rounding, under assumptions supported by profiling experiments. Finally, we develop two prototypes of the learning rate search for a 6.7-billion-parameter model. The first fits the search on a single consumer GPU with 16 GiB of memory. The second speeds up the search on a high-end GPU by evaluating all candidate learning rates in a single pass over the data, so that a five-candidate search takes about half the GPU hours of one full-depth ($k=L$) run.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TipSweep，只训练最后 k0 个 block 来搜索学习率，并给出跨可训练 block 数的精度相关缩放规则，在 1–7B 模型上验证并用分析模型解释 BF16 更新舍入效应。
AI.relevance_reason: 属纯文本后训练超参迁移，与视觉推理无直接关联；但其「最优学习率随深度按 k^{-1} 或 k^{-1/2} 缩放」及低精度更新舍入分析，可能可供核查循环深度或可变有效深度的 latent 推理模型训练。
